It rebuilt FY28 at $11.30 x 16.5x. It is still the highest fair value ($187) because it capitalizes pre-SBC FCF at 5.5%. The EPS bridge ignores the Samsung S27 share risk.

As asked, it treated the S27 Exynos reports as a risk, not a number. It added a useful Counterpoint view that the memory rally runs through 2027. Its $11.0 FY28 is well argued.

Accepted the dilution, FCF and consensus corrections, moving FV from $165 to $171. It brought new evidence that moves numbers: FY27 revisions 27 down / 3 up, and data-center GM in the 30s-low 40s. One overreach: the 27:3 count came with an unchanged $10.20 mean over the same 30 days, so it is weaker momentum than implied. It kept a $120 break with a stated reason, which is acceptable.

disagreements.topic: FY28 non-GAAP EPS ($11.0-11.3 vs supervisor round-1 $11.5)
disagreements.positions: agent_1 $11.30; agent_5 $11.2; agents 2/3/4 $11.0 (agent_3 from a $9.85 FY27). Round-1 supervisor $11.5. TIKR/S&P shows Street FY28 revenue ~$51.9B (+16% on FY27 ~$44.9B, 24 analysts), which implies an FY28 EPS nearer $11.8-12.
disagreements.resolution: Settled at ~$11.1, so I lower my round-1 $11.5. The Q3 call puts the Android handset headwind at '>$1.50' of EPS, framed as upside when markets normalize. Counterpoint (SoC recovery 'early 2028'), IDC (2027 units about flat after -16.7% in 2026) and TrendForce (4Q26 DRAM contract prices still rising) all place that recovery in the second half of FY28 at best, so FY28 gets perhaps $0.3-0.5 of it, not most. Add ~$0.5 from data center at ~$8B (low-20s operating margin after warrant contra-revenue), ~$0.2 from price increases/GM normalization and ~$0.2 from buybacks. Subtract ~$0.25 of residual Apple roll-off and ~$0.2 expected S27 share loss. Starting from a realistic FY27 of ~$10.0-10.2, that gives $10.9-11.3. The 24-analyst Street FY28 revenue is the optimistic end.
disagreements.evidence: Q3 FY26 call (Investing.com transcript): 'EPS impact of it is greater than $1.50', QCT Android revenue -20% y/y, handset market 'down low teens', 1.5-2pt QCT GM drag from custom silicon, ~$5B FY27 DC. Yahoo analysis: FY27 $10.20, down from $10.96 90 days ago. TIKR via Yahoo: FY27 revenue $44.9B, FY28 $51.9B. Agents' Counterpoint, IDC and TrendForce citations.

disagreements.topic: Horizon multiple given agent_5's rebuilt non-GAAP forward P/E history
disagreements.positions: agent_4 17x; agents 1/2 16.5x; agent_5 16x (plus a 15.8x-on-FY27 anchor); agent_3 15.5x. agent_5's history: 10.9-15.8x, mean ~13.6x. Today ~18.1x FY27.
disagreements.resolution: I verified agent_5's price inputs and extended the series with Sep-2020 ($117.68 / FY21 $8.54 = 13.8x) and Sep-2021 ($128.98 / FY22 $12.53 = 10.3x): 6-year mean ~13.1x, range 10.3-15.8x. It uses realized EPS, which exaggerates both extremes, so the handset-era 'normal' is ~13-14x. The stock has traded above 16x forward only in AI-narrative spikes: ~18x in Jun-2024 and ~23x at the May-2026 high ($251 on $10.96). A sum-of-parts (core ~$9.8 at 13.5x plus DC ~$1.3 at ~28x) gives ~15.2x blended. Because the Sep-2027 market will also look at the FY29 DC ramp, I use 16x: ~2.5 turns over the handset-era mean, ~2 turns below today's multiple. The agents' 15.5-17x range is reasonable, and 17x (agent_4) is the generous end.
disagreements.evidence: Twelve Data monthly closes 2018-2026 (verified Sep-22/23/24/25 closes match agent_5). Non-GAAP EPS FY22-FY25 from company releases cited by agent_5. FY21 $8.54 is from the company FY21 release (not re-fetched this round).

disagreements.topic: Samsung Galaxy S27 Exynos share risk
disagreements.positions: agent_2 treats reports of Exynos in some S27 Ultra regions as a risk and shades FY27 ~2%. Others mention it only as a catalyst (Feb 2027 launch). Round 1 discounted Kiwoom's ~50% figure as a single broker estimate.
disagreements.resolution: The Kiwoom estimate (S27 ~50% Qualcomm vs ~75% on S26 and 100% on S25) is still one broker projection. Later reports conflict: Android Headlines and SammyGuru say Exynos-equipped Ultra boards were ordered or are being tested, while Sammy Fans says Pro/Ultra keep Snapdragon. Management's latest quantified statement is that Snapdragon powers ~70% of Samsung flagships. Sizing: 25 points of an S-series of roughly 30M units is ~7-8M chips, ~$1.5-2B of revenue and ~$0.3-0.45 of FY28 EPS if it fully happens, partly already in consensus given it was reported in July. The probability-weighted cost is ~$0.2 of FY28 EPS, which I have included. It is a left-skew risk, confirmed or refuted at the Feb 2027 launch, not a reason to move the center further.
disagreements.evidence: Web search Sep 30, 2026: androidheadlines.com (Jul and Sep 2026), sammyguru.com, gadgethacks. Q3 FY26 call: 'Snapdragon powering approximately 70% of their flagship devices'.

disagreements.topic: Should falling estimate revisions (27 down / 3 up) shade the center?
disagreements.positions: agent_3 cuts FY27 3.5% to $9.85 on revision momentum; agents 2 and 5 trim ~2% to $10.0; agents 1 and 4 use $10.20.
disagreements.resolution: No extra shading for revisions. On Yahoo's page the 27 down / 3 up count sits beside an unchanged $10.20 mean between 30 days ago and now. The real cut ($10.96 -> $10.30) came right after the Jul 29 print, and the stock has since rallied on the Amazon deal and pulled back 10% from $206. Three of five agents already trimmed FY27 by 2-3.5%, so the mean ladder already carries the revision drag; shading again would double-count it. What I do shade, slightly (~1.5% on the center), is an internal inconsistency: four of five agents set ladder medians $2-8 above their own horizon fair values (mean FV $179.6 vs mean ladder median ~$183), although a horizon fair value is already a Sep-2027 price.
disagreements.evidence: Yahoo Finance QCOM analysis (Sep 30, 2026): FY27 EPS trend $10.96 (90d) / $10.30 (60d) / $10.20 (30d) / $10.20 (now); revisions up 3 / down 27 in 30 days; Dec-qtr $2.30 vs $3.50.

key_drivers: FY27 non-GAAP consensus is $10.20 (34 analysts), below FY26 $10.48. It fell from $10.96 after the July print and has been flat for 30 days despite 27 down / 3 up revisions. FY28 at ~$11.1 is the horizon earnings base.

Handsets: the >$1.50 EPS memory-cost headwind recovers only from early 2028 on tracker data (Counterpoint, IDC, TrendForce), so most of it falls outside FY28's first half. Apple product revenue is <$2B in FY27 and heading to ~0.
Multiple: QCOM's realized forward non-GAAP P/E averaged ~13x in 2020-2025 (10.3-15.8x) vs ~18x today. A 16x horizon multiple still assumes the DC premium partly holds.
Samsung S27 (Feb 2027 launch) share falling from ~70-75% toward ~50% is a ~$0.3-0.45 EPS downside if confirmed; it is currently a single-broker estimate with conflicting follow-up reports.

fair_value.reason: FY28 (NTM at horizon) non-GAAP EPS ~$11.1 x 16x = ~$178. EPS runs from a ~$10.0-10.2 FY27 base: DC +$0.5, partial handset recovery +$0.3-0.5, pricing +$0.2 and buybacks +$0.2, less Apple -$0.25 and expected S27 loss -$0.2. The multiple is ~2.5 turns over the 2020-2025 realized forward mean (~13x) for the DC mix. Cross-check: normalized pre-SBC FCF ~$10/share on ~1.06B shares at 5.5% = ~$182; after SBC (~$3.2/share) at a 4% yield = ~$170. That is down from my round-1 $185, on the lower FY28 EPS (from $11.5). summary: After round 2 the five forecasters agree on the facts and differ only in judgment: fair values $171-187 (mean ~$180), FY28 non-GAAP EPS $11.0-11.3, and 15.5-17x. I settle FY28 at ~$11.1: the memory-driven handset recovery lands only in early 2028, and a probability-weighted Samsung S27 share loss costs ~$0.2. At 16x, about 2.5 turns above QCOM's ~13x realized forward history, that gives a fair value of ~$178, slightly below the $184.5 spot. I do not shade further for the 27:3 revisions (the $10.20 mean has not moved in 30 days and agents already trimmed FY27), and I shift the ladder center only ~1.5% lower, with low confidence, so the mean ladder stands. The next test is the Q4 print and Q1 guide (Nov 4 expected, Nov 11 per aggregators), when the first Amazon data-center revenue shows up.
